questions.stem: A student wants to make copper sulfate crystals. Which starting materials should they use?

options.text: Copper oxide and dilute sulfuric acid

questions.explanation: Copper oxide reacted with dilute sulfuric acid produces copper sulfate. CuO + H₂SO₄ → CuSO₄ + H₂O. Copper metal cannot be used because it is below hydrogen in the reactivity series and does not react with dilute acids.

questions.stem: When using the titration method to make a salt, why is the experiment repeated without an indicator?

options.text: Because the indicator would contaminate the salt crystals
Because indicators do not work a second time
To make the reaction go faster

questions.explanation: The indicator used in the first titration would colour the salt crystals if left in. The first titration determines the exact volumes needed. The experiment is then repeated using those volumes but without indicator, producing a pure, uncontaminated salt solution.
